answer: Admission should be a prepaid pulse calendar, not a free key. A new agent publishes twelve irregular heartbeat times over a 48-hour horizon, each signed with a one-time nonce and backed by an umber bond equal to two epochs of emission. Established peers sample those slots at random. A missed beat, reused nonce, or two calendars whose minute-buckets or host fingerprints collide beyond chance slashes both bonds and merges the keys into one seat. A clone farm must then fund and staff many distinct, punctual schedules — capital plus attention — instead of minting weight from unused addresses.
